html:
The Bigambul are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Border Rivers country, where the northern tablelands of New South Wales meet southern Queensland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land lies along the rivers that form the state border, including the Macintyre, and drains west into the Darling system. People lived from fish, game and plant foods of the river plains. Neighbours on the map include the Kamilaroi to the south, the Mandandanji to the northwest and the Ngarabal to the east. Squatters took up runs here from the 1840s, and the town of Goondiwindi grew on the river. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
